To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the social interaction view of agent communication languages is more appropriate than the individual agent view, and (2) this view leads to the conclusion that a new agent communication language, based on the principles of social interaction, is needed.

(1) the current agent communication language (ACL) design principles are insufficient, (2) the ACL design principles should be extended with the following principles: (i) the ACL should support social interaction, (ii) the ACL should be based on a social ontology and (iii) the ACL should allow agents to express their intentions, and (4) the ACL design process should be extended with a new design step, namely the design of social protocols

(1) the agent communication language is not the only problem, but rather a symptom of a more fundamental problem, namely the absence of a shared conceptual model for the agents' communication, and (2) the solution to this problem consists in a shift from a representation of the agents' communication to an explicit representation of the agents and their interaction.
